_comment: What each tool's decoder costs on the device, for the trade-off graph (plot.py): footprint = code + buffers (+ the old file, if plus_old_file), stack excluded. code is .text in bytes, null where no microcontroller build exists (the point is then a lower bound). buffers is RAM the decoder needs besides its stack: dictionaries, windows, caches. stack is recorded but not counted. With plus_old_file, the decoder holds the whole old file in RAM; the graph adds the median old-file size of each kind of data. basis says where each number comes from: measured (bench/decoder-size.sh, Cortex-M0, -Os) or the tool's documentation.

tinydelta.label: tinydelta
tinydelta.basis: measured: callback decoder, Cortex-M0, -Os: 720 B code with arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2; no static RAM or buffers, ~200 B stack

tinydelta_cz_twice.label: tinydelta, compression mode, decoded twice
tinydelta_cz_twice.basis: measured: callback decoder with TINYDELTA_FORMAT_V2=1, Cortex-M0, -Os: 852 B, run twice; no RAM buffers, but the intermediate patch has to be stored, e.g. in external flash

hpatchlite_4k.label: HPatchLite, 4 KB dict.
hpatchlite_4k.basis: code: 662 B for the patch code (HPatchLite README, built with Mbed Studio) plus 1,567 B for the tinyuz decompressor (measured, bench/decoder-size.sh: object code, so possibly including functions a decoder does not call); buffers: one decompression dictionary plus an input cache of at least 3 B (HPatchLite README)

hpatchlite_32k.label: HPatchLite, 32 KB dict.
hpatchlite_32k.basis: as HPatchLite, 4 KB dict., with the default 32 KB dictionary

detools.label: detools (heatshrink)
detools.basis: measured with detools' default heatshrink settings, Cortex-M0: 1,948 B code, no static RAM, ~1.6 KB stack (README benchmark)

bsdiff.label: bsdiff
bsdiff.basis: bzip2 manual: decompressing 900 KB blocks needs about 3.7 MB, or 2.3 MB in small mode; bspatch also holds the old and new file in memory

zstd.label: zstd --patch-from
zstd.basis: zstd --patch-from uses the whole old file as its window, so the decoder needs at least the old file in memory

openvcdiff_interleaved.label: tiny-vcdiff (VCDIFF, interleaved)
openvcdiff_interleaved.basis: measured on a 230 KB MicroPython image (README, decoder footprint notes): tiny-vcdiff linked into a small test program for Cortex-M0, -Os, --gc-sections: 3,881 B code, 3,221 B static RAM, ~150 B stack; it reads open-vcdiff's interleaved format, so its patch sizes are open-vcdiff's with -interleaved

xdelta3.label: xdelta3
xdelta3.basis: xdelta3 keeps the source in memory in blocks (default 8 MB window), which covers the whole old file at these sizes
